clue.text: Rush, we're told, is a weed

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word for rush is heard rather than read

parts.note: to rush is to tear along

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that a rush, the waterside plant, counts as a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like the plant, but it is the verb: to tear along. TEAR, said aloud, sounds like the weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tare is a vetch, a weedy plant of cornfields mentioned in the Bible's parable of wheat and tares.

clue.text: Player in bother is backed by sponsors, primarily — they'll offer a fortune

indicators.note: is backed means the combined letters are read from back to front
in places the player inside the word for bother

parts.note: drat is a mild curse, like bother
a player on stage is an actor

indicators.note: primarily says to use the opening letter of sponsors

explanation.surface: A troubled performer gets financial backing from sponsors who promise riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is backed' reverses DRACTORAT; 'offer a fortune' sounds like money but means telling one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are used in fortune-telling, so they reveal, or offer, one's fortune.

clue.text: Note, celebration involves one displaying finery

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the celebration word wraps around the letter for one

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: At a party, a guest is shown dressed in fine clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems and ceremonial dress of royalty or office, hence splendid finery.

clue.text: Attorney initially rejected case for appeal

parts.note: Att. is the standard abbreviation for attorney

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the word rejected

parts.note: a legal case is an action brought in court

explanation.surface: A lawyer's case is thrown out, leaving him to lodge an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'appeal' look like a court appeal; here it means charm or allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal in the sense of allure or pull is a close synonym of the noun meaning the quality of drawing people in.

clue.text: New star gets involved with cast and performs

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A rising star joins the cast and takes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performs' suggests acting; here it means carries out business.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to carry out or conduct business, so it means to perform a deal.

clue.text: One who loves me to wear jumper

indicators.note: to wear means to have on, so the jumper word goes around the letters of me

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A sweetheart asks me to put on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater; it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, Shakespeare's lover of Juliet, has become a byword for an ardent male lover.

clue.text: Maybe Leo Tolstoy briefly is confused with Lenin, a leader of Communists

indicators.note: leader of says to take the opening letter of Communists
is confused with signals that all these letters are mixed up together
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of Tolstoy is dropped

explanation.surface: Two famous Russians, the novelist and the revolutionary, are mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like Tolstoy's first name, but it is the star sign Leo, the lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the Lion, is one example of a constellation, a named group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Single male first to sprint into pool for dip

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is single

indicators.note: into places that letter inside the pool word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pool

indicators.note: first to says only the opening letter of sprint is used, and that it comes ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: A lone man races to the pool to have a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse something is to plunge it under a liquid, so it means to dip.

clue.text: Duck found on European river

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, nil

explanation.surface: A duck is spotted on a river in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the bird in the picture, but in cricket it means a batter's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great African river flowing north through Egypt to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: A racing event — one on river, say

definitions.text: A racing event — one on river, say

indicators.note: on means the first group of pieces is placed after what follows it in the clue

parts.note: say gives EG, for example
the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
one gives A, as in 'a' meaning one

explanation.surface: A description of a race held on a river, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the first pieces after the river letters; the whole clue doubles as a description. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races, typically held on a river such as the Thames at Henley.

clue.text: Mind you, lies spread about conservationists in a biased way

parts.note: to mind is to look after or tend

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the conservationists
spread says the letters of you and lies are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A warning that lies told about environmentalists are slanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendentiously means in a way that promotes a particular cause or point of view, so with partiality.

clue.text: Portion of vitamin I'm allowed is negligible

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dieter is told how much of a vitamin is permitted: next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minimal is the least possible amount, so slight that it is barely worth counting.

clue.text: One recruits new petrol attendants after dismissing Dan

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are arranged afresh
after dismissing says some letters of the fodder are thrown out before the rearranging

parts.note: the letters of Dan are the ones removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A garage boss hires fresh forecourt staff once Dan has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D, A and N out of PETROL ATTENDANTS and rearrange what is left. Forecourt attendants who fill your tank are now rare in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent spotter seeks out and signs up promising performers or players, so that person recruits.

clue.text: Trembling or shake following ends of seismic event?

definitions.text: Trembling or shake following ends of seismic event?

indicators.note: trembling means shaking, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: ends of says to take the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A description of the tremor that comes after an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of seismic and event give C and T, shuffled with OR SHAKE and F.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a smaller tremor that follows the main shock of an earthquake.

clue.text: A quiet, boring time gets you yawning

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so these letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A dull, silent stretch of time leaves you yawning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it means drilling into: A and P go inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape describes a mouth wide open, as when gaping in wonder or in a yawn.

clue.text: Atoll perhaps cultivated for cereal

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An island is farmed in order to grow grain.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral formation, so it is one example of this structure built by polyps.

clue.text: Rene's gutted, cut up over mark in English test again

indicators.note: over says the reversed piece sits above the next one in this down entry
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the outer letters of Rene
up in a down clue means the word for cut is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Rene is devastated, upset about a grade in an English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' and 'cut up' read as Rene's feelings, but they are working parts of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something a second time is to put it through a fresh check or inspection.

clue.text: Team's oddly beset by failure to secure cup

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so these letters sit inside the word for failure
to secure means to hold fast, reinforcing that the outer word grips the inner letters

parts.note: demise is a downfall or failure

indicators.note: oddly says to take the first, third and fifth characters of Team's

explanation.surface: A sports team's bid for a cup trophy is undone by failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup' suggests a trophy, but it is a small coffee cup. The odd letters of Team's give TAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small coffee cup, its name being French for half a cup.

clue.text: Criminal is more violent around summer time

indicators.note: around places the shuffled letters on either side of the time abbreviation
violent suggests the letters of more are thrown about

parts.note: BST is British Summer Time

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker grows more aggressive during the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a member of a gang of organised criminals, such as the Mafia.

clue.text: Passage requiring a key?

parts.note: a key, as in the Florida Keys, is a low island, which is an isle

explanation.surface: A door or corridor that can only be entered with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' points to locks; here it is a small island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves, a narrow route for people to move along.

clue.text: City wants ballet, but with much more water!

indicators.note: but with says one part of the ballet title is swapped for something else

parts.note: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet
a sea holds much more water than a lake

explanation.surface: A town wants a ballet staged, but with a far wetter set.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in South Wales, on Swansea Bay.

clue.text: CLOSE OFF ROME AND BERLIN?

parts.note: to close off a road is to block it
Rome and Berlin are national capitals

explanation.surface: An order, shouted in upper case, to seal off two European cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed entirely in upper case, which is itself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Block capitals are separate upper-case letters, the style in which this clue is printed.

clue.text: Martial art is to finish in decisive blow

indicators.note: in places the finish word inside the blow abbreviation

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the decisive blow in boxing
to finish is to end

explanation.surface: A fighting discipline's aim is to end a bout with one knockout strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Vulgar supporter upset female

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

explanation.surface: A crude fan has upset a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is informal British slang for tasteless or lacking style, so it means vulgar.

clue.text: Skilled worker is irregular, not punctual at first

indicators.note: not says the following letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: an irregular is a soldier outside the regular army, such as a partisan or guerrilla

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of punctual is used

explanation.surface: A craftsman is erratic and never on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like an adjective describing the worker, but it is a noun: a guerrilla fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson trained in a manual trade, such as a potter or carpenter.

clue.text: Playwright is keeping individual company

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the letters of is surround the next piece

parts.note: an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: A dramatist prefers to stay with one particular person.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was the Romanian-French dramatist of the Theatre of the Absurd, author of Rhinoceros.

clue.text: Case of family retaining no memory — weird, if you ask me

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the outer pair surrounds the shuffled letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
weird signals that the letters of no memory are jumbled

explanation.surface: A household with no recollection is odd, in the speaker's view.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'family' give F and Y; 'weird' shuffles NO MEMORY into ORMYMONE, which they hold.
explanation.definitionFit: For my money is an idiom meaning in my opinion, used to give a personal judgement.

clue.text: Constant request for pin?

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant in science, such as the speed of light
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone keeps asking to borrow a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin' suggests sewing; it is a small barrel, an old beer measure of four and a half gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin is a small beer barrel of about four and a half gallons, so it is one kind of this container.
